subject: Security & Compliance: audit-log retention, BYOK exceptions — sprint input and prioritization
messages:
From: security@trusthealth.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question: short audit retention window for PHI workflows

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team (TrustHealth) has a follow-up ask: for a handful of flows that process PHI we need the ability to set a strict 90-day audit-log retention window and a temporary BYOK flow for escrowed keys during SOC2 review. We want to understand:

- Can Redwood support per-tenant audit-log TTLs (90 days) without elevating product-wide retention?
- Is there a documented exception path for short-window BYOK where keys are escrowed for 30 days with automated deletion?

Attached is our high-level requirements doc. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

—Asha (TrustHealth, Security)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: security@trusthealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: short audit retention window for PHI workflows

Hi Asha / TrustHealth team —

Thanks for the detailed ask and the attachment. Looping in Product (Marissa) and Ops (Priyom) so we can scope feasibility and risk. Initial notes:

- We support per-tenant configuration for metrics/usage TTLs today but audit-log storage is currently a global retention flag tied to our long-term cold store. Implementing per-tenant audit TTL is non-trivial but feasible as a Q1 sprint item if prioritized.
- BYOK escrow: we have an internal pattern used for short-term audits, but it requires an ops play (manual keystore import/export + audit) unless we build a UX+automation flow.

Marissa / Priyom: can you confirm the rough level-of-effort (engineering + infra + compliance review) for: (A) per-tenant audit TTLs (90-day option) and (B) an automated temporary BYOK escrow flow (30-day escrow + auto-delete)?

Proposed next step: 30-minute triage on Friday to align ask -> risk -> timeline.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: short audit retention window for PHI workflows

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 09:34 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hannah —
> 
> Thanks for the detailed ask and the attachment. Looping in Product (Marissa) and Ops (Priyom) so we can scope feasibility and risk. Initial notes:
> 
> - We support per-tenant configuration for metrics/usage TTLs today but audit-log storage is currently a global retention flag tied to our long-term cold store. Implementing per-tenant audit TTL is non-trivial but feasible as a Q1 sprint item if prioritized.
> - BYOK escrow: we have an internal pattern used for short-term audits, but it requires an ops play (manual keystore import/export + audit) unless we build a UX+automation flow.

Team — quick follow-up from Product:

Summary of impact and choices:
- Option A (Low-effort): Documented manual escrow + SOC attestation workflow. No infra changes; relies on ops labor and separate legal sign-off per customer.
- Option B (Medium-effort): Build per-tenant metadata for audit logs and short TTL enforcement; add an admin console toggle and background compaction job. Requires schema changes and migration of old logs to include tenant_id. Estimated 5 sprint-weeks across infra + backend (non-blocking UX).
- Option C (High-effort): Full BYOK escrow automation + per-tenant TTLs, UX for customers to request/approve an escrow window, auto-delete pipeline, and audit reports. Estimated 12 sprint-weeks and cross-team compliance sign-off.

Questions for triage call:
- Which option satisfies TrustHealth's timeline (they flagged audit next-quarter SOC review)?
- If we go with Option A (manual) — what are the documented steps and SLAs for ops handoff?

I'll bring a short PRD sketch to the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Security Integrations
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: short audit retention window for PHI workflows

Hannah / Marissa —

Operational notes from infra/ops POV:

- Per-tenant audit TTL (Option B) work items: add tenant_id index to existing audit-store, add TTL index or lifecycle job to purge logs post-window, and provide retention metadata in Console and API. Risk: migration window could cause temporary increased storage cost and query complexity. Estimated infra effort: 3 sprint-weeks; backend coordination: 2 sprint-weeks.
- Manual escrow (Option A): we can accept customer-provided keys into a locked escrow bucket with HSM-wrapped storage and 30-day retention, but we need documented operator checklists and a customer attestation form. Ops SLA: 3 business days to ingest + 30-day auto-delete job.
- Automation (Option C): would require KMS/HSM integration work, key lifecycle automation, UI, and legal for escrows — estimate 10-12 sprint-weeks.

I'll draft an ops-playbook for Option A if Product asks to go that route as a stopgap. Also raising a Jira: SEC-842 to capture infra tasks (link above).

—Priyom
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: security@trusthealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: short audit retention window for PHI workflows

Hi Asha —

Thanks everyone for quick input. Outcome from triage:

- Immediate path (stopgap): Option A (manual escrow + ops playbook). We will onboard TrustHealth under a documented manual escrow workflow. Ops will accept escrowed keys into a locked store with 30-day retention and produce an attestation report. Priyom to own the ops-playbook and confirm SLA.
- Mid-term path (product): We will scope Option B for Q1 (per-tenant audit TTL + retention metadata in Console) — Marissa to shepherd with infra tickets (SEC-842).
- Long-term: Option C (automation + UX) to be evaluated as part of next quarter roadmap planning.

Action items:
- Priyom: share the ops-playbook draft and attestation template by Tue 17 Nov.
- Marissa: PRD sketch + cost estimate for Option B by Fri 20 Nov.
- Hannah: coordinate legal handshake and send required customer attestation template to Asha.

Asha — please confirm if TrustHealth is ok to proceed with the manual escrow for their SOC review. If yes, we'll send the onboarding checklist and required documents today.

Thanks,
Hannah
